name: Overhead Squat Assessment
description: Global assessment of mobility and stability during an overhead squat.

positive_indicators.lateral: Excessive torso lean, increased lumbar arch

reference: Cook G, Burton L, Hoogenboom BJ, Voight M. Functional movement screening: the use of fundamental movements as an assessment of function - part 1. Int J Sports Phys Ther. 2014;9(3):396-409. PMID: 24944860.
execution: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart
Raise arms overhead with elbows extended
Perform 5-10 controlled squats
Observe from frontal, lateral, and posterior views
Note deviations during descent and ascent
purpose: Screen for global mobility and stability during an overhead squat.
protocol: Observe from: frontal, lateral, posterior.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Single Leg Squat Test
description: Single-leg squat assessment for dynamic knee and hip control.
key_observations: Valgus angle >10 deg indicates a significant deficit

positive_indicators.frontal: Dynamic valgus with contralateral hip drop

execution: Stand on one leg with the other leg forward
Perform a controlled squat to a comfortable depth
Keep the knee tracking over the foot
Observe pelvis and trunk stability
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for Single Leg Squat findings.
protocol: Observe from: frontal.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Drop Jump Landing Test
description: Landing assessment to observe dynamic knee valgus and control.
execution: Stand on a box at a standardized height
Step off and land with both feet
Immediately perform a controlled vertical jump
Observe landing mechanics on the second landing
Repeat for multiple trials
purpose: Screen for Drop Jump Landing findings.
protocol: Observe from: frontal.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Trendelenburg Test
description: Test for gluteus medius function during single-leg stance.

positive_indicators.posterior: Pelvic drop >2 cm on the non-stance side

execution: Stand on one leg with hands on hips
Hold for 10-30 seconds
Observe pelvic drop or trunk shift
Repeat on the other side
Compare stability
purpose: Screen for Trendelenburg findings.
protocol: Observe from: posterior.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Thomas Test
description: Assesses hip flexor length (psoas, rectus femoris, TFL).

positive_indicators.lateral: Thigh elevated (short psoas), knee extended (short rectus femoris)

execution: Lie supine on a table with the pelvis neutral
Pull one knee to the chest
Keep the other leg relaxed on the table
Observe hip extension and knee position
Repeat on the other side
purpose: Screen for Thomas findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Modified Thomas Test
description: Modified version to differentiate specific restrictions.

positive_indicators.lateral: Knee extension suggests rectus femoris tightness, abduction suggests TFL tightness

reference: Thomas (1878); modified version: Kendall FP et al. Muscles: Testing and Function with Posture and Pain. Validity requires pelvic control: Vigotsky AD et al. PeerJ. 2016;4:e2325. Magee DJ. Orthopedic Physical Assessment.
execution: Lie supine at the edge of a table
Pull one knee to the chest to flatten the lumbar spine
Allow the test leg to hang relaxed
Observe thigh position and knee flexion angle
Repeat on the other side
purpose: Screen for Modified Thomas findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Hip Abduction Strength Test
description: Assessment of hip abduction strength (gluteus medius).

positive_indicators.lateral: Unable to hold position, trunk compensation

execution: Lie on the side with the test leg on top
Keep the pelvis stacked and knee straight
Abduct the top leg against manual resistance
Hold 3-5 seconds while resisting
Compare left vs right
purpose: Screen for Hip Abduction Strength findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Pectoralis Major Length Test (Kendall-based)
description: Screens pectoralis major length via passive horizontal abduction/extension with compensation control.
key_observations: Arm cannot approach the support surface (table/floor) during passive horizontal abduction/extension without obvious resistance.
Early compensations appear (shoulder rolls forward/anteriorizes, humerus internally rotates, shoulder elevates/shrugs).
Clear left-right asymmetry in passive end-range or compensatory pattern.

positive_indicators.supine: With the client supine and the examiner passively moving the arm toward horizontal abduction/extension, the arm remains elevated and/or compensations occur (anterior shoulder roll, humeral internal rotation, shoulder elevation) before reaching the expected end-range, especially when asymmetrical side-to-side.

reference: Kendall & McCreary - Muscles: Testing and Function with Posture and Pain (muscle length testing principles; pectoralis major shortness assessed via limitation of shoulder horizontal abduction/extension with compensation control).
execution: Position client supine in hook-lying (knees bent, feet flat) to reduce lumbar compensation; arms relaxed by the sides.
Select the test side. Bring the shoulder to approximately 90 deg abduction with the elbow extended and forearm supinated (palm up).
Passively move the arm slowly toward horizontal abduction/extension (bringing the arm toward the surface behind the frontal plane) without forcing end-range.
Observe for end-range limitation and compensations: anterior shoulder roll/anteriorization, humeral internal rotation, or shoulder elevation/shrugging.
Repeat on the other side and compare symmetry; record the key observations and whether positive indicators were present.
purpose: Screen for passive anterior shoulder restriction patterns consistent with pectoralis major stiffness/shortness within classical muscle length testing.
protocol: Observe from: supine.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Pectoralis Minor Length Test
description: Assesses pectoralis minor length via acromion-to-table distance.
key_observations: Posterior acromion should rest close to the table
Compare sides and note scapular anterior tilt

positive_indicators.supine: Acromion remains elevated off the table or marked asymmetry

reference: Weber C et al. 2016; Harrington SE et al. 2020; Kendall & McCreary - Muscles: Testing and Function with Posture and Pain.
execution: Lie supine with arms relaxed at the sides
Measure acromion-to-table distance at rest
Optional: apply gentle posterior pressure over the coracoid to assess passive length change
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for Pectoralis Minor length findings.
protocol: Observe from: superior.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Lat Length Test
description: Assesses latissimus dorsi length.

positive_indicators.supine: Arms do not reach the surface, back arches

execution: Lie supine with knees bent and low back neutral
Raise both arms overhead toward the floor
Keep ribs down and avoid lumbar extension
Observe whether the arms reach the floor
Compare sides if tested separately
purpose: Screen for Lat Length findings.
protocol: Observe from: supine, lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Scapular Dyskinesis Test
description: Observe scapular motion and position during arm elevation.

positive_indicators.posterior: Winging, asymmetry, lack of upward rotation

execution: Stand with light weights in each hand
Perform repeated shoulder flexion and abduction
Observe scapular winging or asymmetry
View from posterior and lateral angles
Compare left vs right
purpose: Screen for Scapular Dyskinesis findings.
protocol: Observe from: posterior.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Scapular Assistance Test (SAT)
description: Manual assistance into upward rotation; improvement suggests dyskinesis.
key_observations: Pain improvement with assistance indicates a positive test

positive_indicators.lateral: Pain reduction or ROM gain with assistance

execution: Have the client elevate the arm in the scapular plane
Manually assist scapular upward rotation and posterior tilt
Repeat the arm elevation with assistance
Note changes in pain or range
Compare to the unassisted movement
purpose: Screen for Scapular Assistance findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Lateral Scapular Slide Test
description: Measure bilateral scapular position symmetry.
key_observations: Measure distance from scapular spine to spine
execution: Stand relaxed with arms at the sides
Measure scapular position relative to the spine
Repeat with hands on hips (45 deg abduction)
Repeat with arms abducted to 90 deg
Compare left vs right distances
purpose: Screen for Lateral Scapular Slide findings.
protocol: Observe from: posterior.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Wall Test (FHP)
description: Assesses forward head posture against a wall.

positive_indicators.lateral: Unable to touch wall with the occiput without forcing

execution: Stand with heels, hips, and upper back against a wall
Keep the chin level and eyes forward
Check if the occiput touches the wall
Measure the occiput-to-wall distance
Document the distance
purpose: Screen for Wall findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Chin Tuck Test
description: Assesses activation of deep cervical flexors.

positive_indicators.lateral: Unable to retract, flexion compensation

execution: Sit or stand tall with the head in neutral
Glide the chin straight back to make a double chin
Keep eyes level and avoid head tilt
Hold for 3-5 seconds
Repeat for multiple reps and note control
purpose: Screen for Chin Tuck findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Craniocervical Flexion Test (CCFT)
description: Assesses endurance of deep cervical flexors with biofeedback.

positive_indicators.supine: Unable to hold pressure, SCM compensation

execution: Lie supine with knees bent and head supported
Gently nod the chin as if saying "yes" without lifting the head
Maintain the nod while lifting the head slightly
Hold for the prescribed time or pressure target
Monitor for loss of chin tuck or compensations
purpose: Screen for Craniocervical Flexion findings.
protocol: Observe from: supine.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Cervical Rotation ROM
description: Assesses active and passive cervical rotation.
reference: Williams MA et al. Reliability and validity of cervical ROM measurement methods. J Manipulative Physiol Ther. 2010;33(2):138-155. CROM and inclinometer show good reliability.
execution: Sit or stand tall with shoulders relaxed
Slightly tuck the chin
Rotate the head to one side as far as comfortable
Avoid shoulder elevation or trunk rotation
Repeat on the other side and compare
purpose: Screen for Cervical Rotation ROM findings.
protocol: Observe from: superior.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Flexion-Rotation Test
description: Specific for C1-C2 dysfunction.
execution: Lie supine with knees bent
Passively flex the cervical spine
Maintain full flexion and rotate the head left and right
Observe end range and symptom reproduction
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for Flexion-Rotation findings.
protocol: Observe from: supine.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Seated Thoracic Rotation Test
description: Assesses thoracic rotation in seated position.
key_observations: Seated to lock the lumbar spine
reference: Joint Range of Motion and Muscle Length Testing
execution: Sit upright with arms crossed over the chest
Keep the pelvis stable and rotate the torso
Rotate left and right to end range
Measure or estimate the rotation angle
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for Seated Thoracic Rotation findings.
protocol: Observe from: superior.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
description: Assesses thoracic rotation in quadruped.
execution: Assume a quadruped position with spine neutral
Place one hand behind the head
Rotate the thorax toward the ceiling
Keep hips level and lumbar stable
Compare left vs right rotation
purpose: Screen for Quadruped Thoracic Rotation findings.
protocol: Observe from: frontal.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Thoracic Kyphosis Measurement
description: Measure thoracic kyphosis using a flexicurve or inclinometer.

positive_indicators.lateral: Increased kyphosis with a prominent apex

execution: Stand relaxed with arms at sides
Mold the flexicurve along the thoracic spine
Trace the curve on paper or measure directly
Calculate or estimate the kyphosis angle
Document the value
purpose: Screen for Thoracic Kyphosis Measurement findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Shoulder Internal Rotation at 90 deg Abduction
description: Assesses glenohumeral internal rotation (GIRD).

positive_indicators.supine: Loss >15 deg compared to contralateral side indicates GIRD

reference: Joint Range of Motion and Muscle Length Testing
execution: Lie supine with shoulder abducted to 90 deg
Flex the elbow to 90 deg and stabilize the scapula
Rotate the forearm toward the table into internal rotation
Stop before the shoulder lifts
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for Shoulder Internal Rotation at 90 deg Abduction findings.
protocol: Observe from: supine.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Sleeper Stretch Tolerance
description: Assesses posterior capsule tolerance and restriction.

positive_indicators.lateral: Pain or restriction compared to the other side

execution: Lie on the side of the test shoulder
Set the shoulder and elbow at 90 deg
Stabilize the scapula against the surface
Gently internally rotate the arm
Note end range and tolerance
purpose: Screen for Sleeper Stretch Tolerance findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Neer Impingement Test
description: Assesses subacromial impingement.
key_observations: Passive flexion with the scapula stabilized
execution: Stand with the arm internally rotated (thumb down)
Passively flex the arm overhead in the scapular plane
Stabilize the scapula to limit upward rotation
Note pain near end range
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for Neer Impingement findings.
protocol: Observe from: frontal.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Hawkins-Kennedy Test
description: Assesses subacromial impingement.
key_observations: Shoulder flexion 90 deg with forced internal rotation
execution: Elevate the arm to 90 deg of shoulder flexion
Flex the elbow to 90 deg
Stabilize the shoulder and internally rotate the arm
Observe pain or apprehension
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for Hawkins-Kennedy findings.
protocol: Observe from: frontal.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Empty Can (Jobe) Test
description: Assesses supraspinatus integrity.
key_observations: Arms at 90 deg abduction, 30 deg horizontal, thumbs down
Weakness or pain indicates a positive test
execution: Stand with arms elevated in the scapular plane to 90 deg
Internally rotate so thumbs point down
Apply downward pressure at the distal forearm
Ask the client to resist the pressure
Note pain or weakness compared to the other side
purpose: Screen for Empty Can findings.
protocol: Observe from: frontal.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Painful Arc Test
description: Pain between 60-120 deg of abduction suggests impingement.
key_observations: Pain in the mid-range of abduction
execution: Stand with arms relaxed at sides
Slowly abduct the arm through the full range
Note the range where pain appears or resolves
Repeat on the opposite side
Document the painful arc range
purpose: Screen for Painful Arc findings.
protocol: Observe from: frontal.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Lumbar Lordosis Assessment
description: Measurement of lumbar lordosis.

positive_indicators.lateral: Hyperlordosis (>60 deg) or hypolordosis (<40 deg)

execution: Stand relaxed in neutral stance
Identify lumbar landmarks (L1 and S1)
Measure curvature with an inclinometer or visual estimate
Note excessive lordosis or flattening
Document angle or observation
purpose: Screen for Lumbar Lordosis findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Pelvic Tilt Visual Assessment
description: Visual assessment of pelvic tilt and posture.
key_observations: ASIS lower than PSIS indicates APT
ASIS higher than PSIS indicates PPT

positive_indicators.lateral: Deviation from neutral (ASIS 0-10 deg lower than PSIS)

execution: Stand in a relaxed neutral stance
View from the side at pelvis level
Compare ASIS and PSIS alignment
Note anterior or posterior tilt
Document findings
purpose: Screen for Pelvic Tilt Visual findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Prone Hip Extension Test
description: Assessment of gluteal activation and hip extension pattern.

positive_indicators.posterior: Hamstring or erector activates before the glute

execution: Lie prone with legs straight
Activate glute and lift one leg slightly
Keep the pelvis level and avoid lumbar extension
Observe timing of glute vs hamstring activation
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for Prone Hip Extension findings.
protocol: Observe from: posterior.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: McGill Core Endurance Tests
description: McGill core endurance tests for trunk stability.

positive_indicators.lateral: Asymmetry or abnormal ratios

execution: Perform the trunk flexor endurance test (modified curl-up hold)
Perform the trunk extensor endurance test (Sorensen hold)
Perform right and left side bridge holds
Record time to fatigue for each test
Compare ratios and side-to-side differences
purpose: Screen for McGill Core Endurance Tests findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Prone Instability Test
description: Assesses lumbar instability.
key_observations: Pain that improves with extensor activation
execution: Lie prone with the trunk on a table and feet on the floor
Apply posterior-to-anterior pressure to the lumbar spine
Have the client lift the legs off the floor
Reapply pressure to the lumbar spine
Compare symptoms between positions
purpose: Screen for Prone Instability findings.
protocol: Observe from: posterior.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Active Straight Leg Raise (ASLR)
description: Assesses lumbopelvic stability and hamstring length.
key_observations: Ability to raise the leg without compensation

positive_indicators.lateral: Pelvic rotation or difficulty lifting

execution: Lie supine with both legs straight and arms at sides
Keep the non-test leg flat and toes up
Raise the test leg with the knee straight as high as possible
Stop before the pelvis tilts or the other leg lifts
Compare left vs right range
purpose: Screen for Active Straight Leg Raise findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Slump Test
description: Assesses neural tension.

positive_indicators.lateral: Reproduction of radicular pain

execution: Sit upright on the edge of a table
Slump the spine and flex the neck
Extend the knee and dorsiflex the ankle
Observe symptom reproduction or relief with head position
Repeat on the other side
purpose: Screen for Slump findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Ely Test (Rectus Femoris)
description: Specific for rectus femoris length.
key_observations: Pelvic rise indicates a positive test

positive_indicators.lateral: Pelvis lifts with knee flexion

execution: Lie prone with legs straight
Stabilize the pelvis to prevent anterior tilt
Flex the test knee, bringing the heel toward the glute
Observe hip lift or pelvic rotation
Compare left vs right
purpose: Screen for Ely findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Knee-to-Wall (Weight-Bearing Lunge) Test
description: Weight-bearing lunge test for ankle dorsiflexion.
key_observations: Toe-to-wall distance with the knee touching

positive_indicators.lateral: <10 cm or bilateral asymmetry

execution: Face a wall in a split stance
Keep the test heel on the floor
Drive the knee toward the wall without heel lift
Measure the maximum distance or knee-to-wall gap
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for Knee-to-Wall findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Gastrocnemius vs Soleus Differentiation
description: Differentiates gastrocnemius vs soleus restriction.

positive_indicators.lateral: Restriction with knee extended (gastroc) or flexed (soleus)

reference: Silfverskiöld test. DiGiovanni CW et al. Foot Ankle Int. 2014;35(8):838-844. DOI: 10.1177/1071100714535202.
execution: Measure ankle dorsiflexion with the knee straight
Repeat the measurement with the knee bent
Compare straight vs bent knee values
Note which condition is more limited
Compare left vs right
purpose: Screen for Gastrocnemius vs Soleus Differentiation findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Navicular Drop Test
description: Assesses foot pronation.
key_observations: Measure navicular height seated vs standing
execution: Find and mark the navicular tuberosity
Measure navicular height in seated neutral foot
Stand and measure navicular height again
Calculate the drop between seated and standing
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for Navicular Drop findings.
protocol: Observe from: medial.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Single Leg Heel Raise Test
description: Assesses gastrocnemius-soleus strength and endurance.
execution: Stand on one leg near support
Rise onto the ball of the foot with full plantarflexion
Lower under control and repeat to fatigue
Count total reps or time
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for Single Leg Heel Raise findings.
protocol: Observe from: posterior.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Windlass Test
description: Specific for plantar fasciitis.
key_observations: Pain reproduction indicates a positive test

positive_indicators.medial: Pain in the plantar fascia with great toe extension

execution: Sit or stand with the foot relaxed
Extend the big toe passively
Observe arch formation and symptoms
Note pain at the medial heel or arch
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for Windlass findings.
protocol: Observe from: medial.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Hip External Rotation at 90 deg Flexion
description: Assesses hip external rotation.
key_observations: Restriction suggests posterior capsule or piriformis
reference: Joint Range of Motion and Muscle Length Testing
execution: Lie supine with hip and knee at 90 deg
Stabilize the pelvis
Move the lower leg inward to create hip external rotation
Stop at end range without pelvic tilt
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for Hip External Rotation at 90 deg Flexion findings.
protocol: Observe from: supine.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Push-Up Assessment
description: Assesses scapular and core control during a push-up.

positive_indicators.lateral: Loss of plank position, hips sagging

execution: Start in a plank position with hands under shoulders
Perform controlled push-ups to a consistent depth
Observe trunk alignment and scapular control
Note compensations such as sagging or winging
Repeat 3-5 reps
purpose: Screen for trunk and scapular control during a push-up.
protocol: Observe from: lateral, superior.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Goblet Squat Assessment
description: Squat assessment with anterior load to observe movement compensations.

positive_indicators.lateral: Excessive lean, butt wink

execution: Hold a light kettlebell or dumbbell at the chest
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart
Squat to depth with a controlled tempo
Observe knee tracking, trunk angle, and foot stability
Repeat 3-5 reps
purpose: Screen for squat mechanics with an anterior load.
protocol: Observe from: frontal, lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Single Leg Deadlift Assessment
description: Single-leg deadlift assessment for hip hinge control.

positive_indicators.lateral: Loss of neutral spine

execution: Stand on one leg with a soft knee
Hinge at the hip as the free leg reaches back
Keep the spine neutral and hips square
Return to standing with control
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for single-leg hinge control and balance.
protocol: Observe from: lateral, posterior.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Shoulder Press Assessment
description: Shoulder press assessment to observe thoracic and shoulder mobility.
key_observations: Lockout with arms by the ears

positive_indicators.lateral: Excessive lumbar arch, arms forward of the ears

execution: Stand with a light load or dowel
Press overhead in a controlled manner
Maintain rib position and neutral spine
Observe scapular control and shoulder symmetry
Repeat 3-5 reps
purpose: Screen for overhead pressing mechanics and shoulder control.
protocol: Observe from: lateral, frontal.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Cervical Sidebending ROM
description: Assessment of cervical sidebending range of motion.
key_observations: Pain or stiffness at end range

positive_indicators.frontal: Marked asymmetry or pain during sidebending

reference: Joint Range of Motion and Muscle Length Testing
execution: Sit tall with shoulders relaxed
Keep the nose and chin facing forward
Side-bend the head toward the shoulder
Avoid rotation or shoulder hiking
Repeat on the other side
purpose: Screen for Cervical Sidebending ROM findings.
protocol: Observe from: frontal.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Lumbar Flexion ROM
description: Assessment of lumbar flexion range of motion.
key_observations: Pain or stiffness at end range

positive_indicators.lateral: Restricted lumbar flexion or marked hip compensation

reference: Joint Range of Motion and Muscle Length Testing
execution: Stand with feet hip-width apart
Slowly bend forward to touch the floor
Keep knees straight without bouncing
Measure reach or spine angle
Compare to normative values
purpose: Screen for Lumbar Flexion ROM findings.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Ober Test
target: Assess TFL and IT band tightness
description: Classic test to evaluate tensor fasciae latae and iliotibial band tension. Positive if the leg fails to drop to horizontal.
execution: Lie on the side with the test leg on top
Stabilize the pelvis to prevent tilt
Extend and abduct the test hip
Allow the leg to adduct toward the table
Observe if the thigh drops past midline
interpretation: Negative: leg drops to horizontal or below
Positive: leg remains abducted (short TFL/IT band)

positive_indicators.side: Thigh remains abducted or pelvis tilts

purpose: Screen for Ober findings.
protocol: Observe from: side.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: FABER/Patrick Test
target: Assess hip pathology, SI joint, and hip flexor restrictions
description: Screening test for the hip and sacroiliac joint. FABER stands for Flexion, Abduction, External Rotation. Pain location helps identify the source.
execution: Lie supine with the pelvis neutral
Place the test ankle above the opposite knee (figure-4)
Stabilize the opposite pelvis
Gently press the test knee toward the table
Compare range and discomfort to the other side
cues: Ask for the exact pain location
interpretation: Groin pain: possible intra-articular hip pathology
ROM limitation without pain: muscular stiffness

positive_indicators.supine: Increased distance or reproduction of hip/SI pain

purpose: Screen for FABER/Patrick findings.
protocol: Observe from: supine.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Apley Scratch Test
description: Quick screening test for shoulder ROM. Assesses combined movements in two patterns.
execution: Stand tall with relaxed shoulders
Reach one hand over the same-side shoulder toward the upper back
Reach the other hand behind the back and up toward the shoulder blades
Measure the distance between fingertips or note overlap
Repeat on the opposite side
cues: Reach as far as possible without pain
interpretation: Pattern 1 limited: internal rotation, extension, or adduction
Pattern 2 limited: external rotation, flexion, or abduction
reference: David J. Magee - Orthopedic Physical Assessment
key_observations: Distance between the hands behind the back

positive_indicators.posterior: Large asymmetry or inability to approximate hands

purpose: Screen for Apley Scratch findings.
protocol: Observe from: posterior.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Y-Balance Test / Star Excursion
target: Assess dynamic balance, neuromuscular control, and asymmetries
description: Gold-standard test to assess dynamic balance and detect asymmetries that predict injury risk. Simplified version of the Star Excursion Balance Test.
execution: Stand on the test leg at the center point
Reach the free leg in the anterior direction
Reach in posteromedial and posterolateral directions
Maintain balance without touching down
Record reach distances and compare sides
cues: Touch lightly, do not load the reaching foot
interpretation: Asymmetry >4 cm between legs indicates higher injury risk
Anterior reach <65% of leg length indicates higher risk
Posterolateral deficit suggests glute med or lateral core weakness
key_observations: Reach distance in anterior, posteromedial, posterolateral directions

positive_indicators.frontal: Large asymmetry or loss of balance

purpose: Screen for dynamic balance and reach asymmetry.
protocol: Observe from: frontal.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Postural Assessment
description: Global standing postural scan to identify alignment deviations.

positive_indicators.frontal: Asymmetry in shoulders, pelvis, or knees
positive_indicators.lateral: Forward head, rounded shoulders, or pelvic tilt deviations
positive_indicators.posterior: Scapular winging, spinal deviation, or pelvic shift

reference: Kendall FP, McCreary EK, Provance PG. Muscles: Testing and Function with Posture and Pain. Lippincott. Postural alignment and plumb line assessment.
execution: Have the client stand relaxed and barefoot
Assess from the sagittal view first
Assess from the frontal and posterior views
Note head, shoulder, spine, pelvic, knee, and foot alignment
Document asymmetries and deviations
purpose: Screen for postural alignment deviations.
protocol: Observe from: frontal, lateral, posterior.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Postural Assessment (Side View)
description: Lateral postural scan emphasizing sagittal alignment.
key_observations: Ear over shoulder, shoulder over hip

positive_indicators.lateral: Forward head, rounded shoulders, or excessive kyphosis/lordosis

reference: Kendall FP et al. Muscles: Testing and Function with Posture and Pain. Sagittal postural alignment (lateral view).
execution: Stand relaxed with feet together
View the client from the lateral side
Check ear-shoulder-hip-knee-ankle alignment
Note forward head, kyphosis, or pelvic tilt
Document deviations
purpose: Screen for sagittal plane postural deviations.
protocol: Observe from: lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Squat Assessment
description: Uncoached bodyweight squat to observe habitual movement patterns.

positive_indicators.lateral: Excessive forward lean or lumbar extension

reference: Cook G, Burton L, Hoogenboom BJ, Voight M. Functional movement screening: the use of fundamental movements as an assessment of function - part 1. Int J Sports Phys Ther. 2014;9(3):396-409. PMID: 24944860.
execution: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart
Perform a bodyweight squat without coaching
Observe from frontal, lateral, and posterior views
Note knee alignment, trunk angle, and foot control
Repeat 5-10 reps
purpose: Screen for movement compensations during a bodyweight squat.
protocol: Observe from: frontal, lateral, posterior.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Overhead Reach Assessment
description: Standing overhead reach to screen shoulder mobility and compensations.
key_observations: Ability to raise arms overhead without trunk compensation

positive_indicators.lateral: Forward head or lumbar extension during reach

reference: Functional shoulder mobility assessment. Apley scratch test (Hoppenfeld). Orthopedic shoulder examination standard.
execution: Stand tall with feet together
Raise both arms overhead with thumbs up
Keep ribs down and neck neutral
Observe scapular control and trunk compensation
Compare left vs right reach
purpose: Screen for Overhead Reach findings.
protocol: Observe from: frontal, lateral.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Big Toe Extension Assessment
description: Assesses big toe extension range of motion.

positive_indicators.medial: Extension less than 70 degrees or side-to-side asymmetry

reference: First MTPJ extension / windlass. Hicks JH. J Anat. 1953;87:345-357. Jack's test, FHL: López et al. Foot Ankle Int. 2020;41(4):457-462. PMID: 31994419.
execution: Sit with the foot supported and ankle in neutral
Stabilize the midfoot and heel
Extend the big toe upward as far as possible
Estimate or measure the extension angle
Compare left vs right
purpose: Screen for Big Toe Extension findings.
protocol: Observe from: medial.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Foot Inversion Assessment
description: Assesses ability to invert the foot and control pronation.
key_observations: Ability to invert the foot with knee extended

positive_indicators.frontal: Unable to reach neutral inversion or excessive pronation

reference: Subtalar/inversion assessment. Elveru RA et al. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther. 1994;19(3):162-167. Picciano AM et al. JOSPT. 1993;18(4):553-558.
execution: Stand in a split stance with the test foot forward
Keep the test knee extended
Invert the test foot as far as possible
Observe if the forefoot reaches neutral or beyond
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for Foot Inversion findings.
protocol: Observe from: frontal.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: TFL Frontal Plane Assessment
description: Frontal plane check during modified Thomas position to assess TFL stiffness.
key_observations: Thigh alignment relative to the trunk
Abduction at rest indicating TFL shortening

positive_indicators.frontal: Thigh abducts away from midline at rest

reference: TFL/hip flexor differentiation in modified Thomas. Kendall FP et al. Muscles: Testing and Function with Posture and Pain. Ober test: Gajdosik RL et al. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther. 2003;33(6):326-330. PMID: 12839207.
execution: Set the client in the modified Thomas position
View the test leg from the frontal plane
Observe thigh alignment relative to the trunk
Note abduction at rest indicating TFL stiffness
Compare sides
purpose: Screen for TFL Frontal Plane findings.
protocol: Observe from: frontal.
Standardize start position and instructions.
Perform 2-3 trials per side when applicable.
Record key observations and any positive indicators.
Compare left vs right when applicable.

name: Cozen's Test
description: Resisted wrist extension test for lateral epicondylalgia.
key_observations: Pain at lateral epicondyle with resisted wrist extension

positive_indicators.lateral: Reproduction of lateral elbow pain with resisted wrist extension

execution: Patient makes a fist with the elbow extended
Therapist applies resistance to wrist extension and radial deviation
Ask for pain location and intensity
purpose: Screen for lateral epicondylalgia.
protocol: Compare both sides
Record pain location and severity
Use with other tests for confirmation

name: Mill's Test
description: Passive stretch test for lateral epicondylalgia.
key_observations: Pain at lateral epicondyle with passive wrist flexion and elbow extension

positive_indicators.lateral: Reproduction of lateral elbow pain during passive stretch

execution: Patient seated with elbow extended and forearm pronated
Therapist passively flexes the wrist and flexes the fingers
Ask for pain location and intensity
purpose: Screen for lateral epicondylalgia.
protocol: Compare both sides
Avoid excessive force
Document pain location

name: Maudsley's Test (Resisted Middle Finger)
description: Resisted middle finger extension test for lateral epicondylalgia.
key_observations: Pain at lateral epicondyle with resisted middle finger extension

positive_indicators.lateral: Reproduction of lateral elbow pain during resisted middle finger extension

execution: Patient extends the middle finger
Therapist applies resistance
Ask for pain location and intensity
purpose: Screen for lateral epicondylalgia.
protocol: Compare both sides
Record pain intensity
Use with other tests

name: Pain-Free Grip Strength Test
description: Grip strength recorded at pain-free threshold for epicondylalgia tracking.

positive_indicators.anterior: Reduced pain-free grip strength on affected side

execution: Patient squeezes dynamometer until pain threshold
Record the force reading
Repeat 2-3 trials
purpose: Monitor symptom-limited grip strength.
protocol: Use consistent position and dynamometer setting
Average 2-3 trials
Compare to contralateral side

name: Medial Epicondyle Tenderness
description: Palpation of medial epicondyle and flexor-pronator origin.

positive_indicators.medial: Pain with palpation at the medial epicondyle

execution: Patient seated with elbow flexed
Palpate the medial epicondyle and flexor origin
Ask for pain rating
purpose: Screen for medial epicondylalgia.
protocol: Compare both sides
Document pain location

name: Resisted Wrist Flexion/Pronation Test
description: Resisted wrist flexion and forearm pronation test for medial epicondylalgia.
key_observations: Pain at medial epicondyle with resisted flexion/pronation

positive_indicators.medial: Reproduction of medial elbow pain during resisted flexion/pronation

execution: Patient flexes wrist and pronates forearm
Therapist applies resistance
Ask for pain location and intensity
purpose: Screen for medial epicondylalgia.
protocol: Compare both sides
Record pain intensity
Use with palpation findings

name: Wrist Extension ROM
description: Active wrist extension range of motion assessment.

positive_indicators.lateral: Limited or painful wrist extension

execution: Forearm supported with palm down
Patient actively extends the wrist
Compare to contralateral side
purpose: Identify limitation in wrist extension range.
protocol: Standardize elbow position
Compare left vs right
Record pain and end range

name: Wrist Flexion ROM
description: Active wrist flexion range of motion assessment.

positive_indicators.lateral: Limited or painful wrist flexion

execution: Forearm supported with palm up
Patient actively flexes the wrist
Compare to contralateral side
purpose: Identify limitation in wrist flexion range.
protocol: Standardize elbow position
Compare left vs right
Record pain and end range

name: Forearm Pronation ROM
description: Active forearm pronation range of motion assessment.
execution: Elbow at 90 degrees with forearm supported
Patient rotates palm down
Compare to contralateral side
purpose: Identify limitation in forearm pronation range.
protocol: Keep elbow fixed at 90 degrees
Compare left vs right
Record pain and end range

name: Forearm Supination ROM
description: Active forearm supination range of motion assessment.
execution: Elbow at 90 degrees with forearm supported
Patient rotates palm up
Compare to contralateral side
purpose: Identify limitation in forearm supination range.
protocol: Keep elbow fixed at 90 degrees
Compare left vs right
Record pain and end range

name: Elbow Valgus Stress Test
description: Assesses medial elbow stability under valgus stress.
key_observations: Pain or laxity at medial elbow

positive_indicators.medial: Pain or increased laxity with valgus stress

execution: Patient supine or seated with elbow slightly flexed
Apply valgus stress to the elbow
Assess pain and end feel
purpose: Screen for medial elbow instability.
protocol: Compare both sides
Stop if sharp pain occurs
